strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies and demonstrates how existing motion customization methods fail on distilled video generators due to collapsed denoising trajectories—a genuine limitation at the intersection of knowledge distillation and motion control.

Technically sound and novel solution: Teacher-guided trajectory correction with adaptive acceleration strategy is mathematically principled and creative. The adaptive scheduling mechanism that monitors motion loss to dynamically decide teacher guidance is particularly elegant.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive evaluation across multiple distilled models (T2V-Turbo-V2, Video-Blade, Wan2.1, CogVideoX-2B), three benchmarks (TurboBench, DavisBench, LOVEU-TGVE), multiple metrics, ablation studies, and user study with 50 participants. Computational analysis demonstrates practical feasibility.

Architecture-agnostic design: Method works with different motion extractors (MotionClone, MotionDirector, MOFT, DMVT) and diffusion backbones, demonstrating genuine generality and practical applicability.

Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Clear problem visualization, well-organized methodology with intuitive pipeline diagram, complete algorithmic description (Algorithm 1), extensive hyperparameter documentation, and commitment to release code. Mathematical derivations are rigorous.

Practical value without retraining: Training-free approach enables efficient motion control on existing distilled models without requiring model retraining or fine-tuning, making it immediately applicable.

Meaningful limitations discussion: Acknowledges shortcomings (object-motion misalignment, fine-grained control), discusses future work directions, and includes thoughtful treatment of ethical concerns regarding misuse potential.
weaknesses: Teacher model dependency at inference: Requires access to full, non-distilled teacher model during inference, limiting applicability when teachers are unavailable, proprietary, or resource-constrained. Offline caching of teacher guidance is not explored.

Limited failure case analysis: While one failure case is shown (Figure 8), systematic analysis of failure modes is lacking. Questions remain about when adaptive scheduling incorrectly terminates guidance, which motion types are challenging, and degradation with minimal teacher steps.

Inference cost remains substantial: TurboV2 requires 7-13s (vs. 7s baseline) and Video-Blade requires 23-55s (vs. ~20s baseline). For a method targeting 'fast' generators, this overhead is meaningful and could use more thorough discussion of quality-speed trade-offs.

Limited exploration of out-of-distribution motions: All experiments use natural reference videos. Method is not evaluated on synthesized motions, extreme camera movements, physically impossible transitions, or other creative scenarios that may appear in real applications.

Hyperparameter tuning guidance: While ablations show robustness (Tables 4-5), practical guidance for setting λ, η, δ₁, δ₂, W, N_min on new datasets/models is limited. Sensitivity analysis focuses primarily on TurboV2.

Fixed score interpolation weight: Equation 5 uses constant interpolation weight to control guidance strength—a somewhat simplistic approach. Adaptive weighting per timestep might improve quality-efficiency trade-off.
User study design details: 50 participants is adequate, but inter-rater agreement metrics and statistical significance testing details would strengthen perceptual quality claims.
